column2: Cheap worn synthetic carpet in a low-rent apartment. Flat mid-grey-brown with a faint short pile texture, traffic-worn patches, a few old stains ground in. Utterly unglamorous.
Small square ceramic bathroom tiles, roughly 15cm each so many per tile, off-white going grey, grout lines darkened with age and mildew, a couple of chipped tiles.
Poured concrete corridor floor, sealed and scuffed, visible aggregate, faint control joints, scattered scratches and dark scuff marks from decades of foot traffic.
Cheap vinyl sheet flooring in a fake pale-grey stone pattern, curling and lifted in places, cigarette burns and dark grease marks near where a cooker would be.

Polished dark grey-green marble floor in an expensive corporate tower lobby, large format slabs roughly 1m square with fine pale veining and tight joints, buffed to a soft sheen. Immaculately maintained — this is a rich building, NOT grimy. Keep it dark enough that light tokens read on top.

Dense low-pile commercial carpet in a corporate meeting room, deep charcoal with a subtle darker geometric weave, clean and well kept, faint vacuum tracks. Expensive and understated, not patterned or loud.

Small polished marble floor tiles in a luxury washroom, roughly 30cm each so many per tile, pale warm grey with darker veining, narrow clean grout lines, slight wet sheen. Spotless — an expensive building, no mildew or damage.
Dark stained hardwood strip flooring in an upmarket residents' bar, narrow boards running one direction, rich brown with visible grain and a satin lacquer, lightly worn along the traffic line.

Top-down interior courtyard garden floor: dark planting soil and fine bark mulch with patches of low clipped ground cover and moss, threaded with pale flagstone paving. Lush and deliberately landscaped, softly lit.

Top-down surface of a lit indoor swimming pool, clear turquoise water over pale tiling, gentle surface ripples with soft caustic light patterns, slight depth gradient. No pool edge, no coping, no people — water surface only.
